body:
### Description

### Description

We have a C++ project which the GitHub Action runner compiles (within a docker container, which has been unchanged for months).  Normally, this builds fine (and continues to the next step in our workflow).  After the latest ubuntu-24.04 image update, the CI build step running the compilation is hanging.

The failed build eventually times out (after no terminal updates about 1 minute into compilation), reporting
> The hosted runner lost communication with the server. Anything in your workflow that terminates the runner process, starves it for CPU/Memory, or blocks its network access can cause this error.

We retried the builds with similar effect.

We have verified that the code is unchanged from the working build on the previous runner image.

In previously filed issue #13182, the same symptoms occurred on the same repositories as in the current issue. title: [Ubuntu 24.04] podman broken on 20260726.254: uses /usr/bin/crun 1.14.1 instead of the crun 1.28 in /usr/local/bin
body:
### Description

Every `podman run` and `podman build` fails on the ubuntu-24.04 image with:

```
Error: OCI runtime error: crun: unknown version specified
```

The image has podman 5.8.4 and crun 1.28, but podman is not using that crun. It resolves the runtime to `/usr/bin/crun`, which is still the Ubuntu archive build at 1.14.1:

```
$ podman --version
podman version 5.8.4
$ podman info --format '{{.Host.OCIRuntime.Path}}'
/usr/bin/crun
$ /usr/bin/crun --version
crun version 1.14.1
$ /usr/local/bin/crun --version
crun version 1.28
$ command -v crun
/usr/local/bin/crun
```

podman 5.8.4 writes `"ociVersion":"1.2.1"` into config.json. crun 1.14.1 rejects any version string that does not contain "1.0" (src/libcrun/container.c at the 1.14.1 tag):

```c
if (def->ociVersion && strstr (def->ociVersion, "1.0") == NULL)
    return crun_make_error (err, 0, "unknown version specified");
```

so nothing starts. crun dropped that check in 1.16.

One thing that makes this annoying to debug: `crun --version` reports 1.28, because /usr/local/bin comes first on PATH. It looks like a current crun is installed while podman is actually running the old one.

Installing crun 1.28 over /usr/bin/crun fixes it. I confirmed that on a runner that had the broken image.

### Platforms affected

- [x] GitHub Actions - Standard Runners

### Runner images affected

- [x] Ubuntu 24.04

### Image version and build link

Version: 20260726.254.1

https://github.com/actions/runner-images/releases/tag/ubuntu24%2F20260726.254

### Is it regression?

Yes. Image 20260720.247.2 works. It has podman 4.9.3, which writes ociVersion 1.0.x, and crun 1.14.1 accepts that. The podman 4.9.3 to 5.8.4 bump is the only container change listed in the release notes for 20260726.254.

Because the rollout is staged, jobs currently pass or fail depending on which image they get. The same commit can pass and fail minutes apart, which is how this first showed up for me.

ubuntu-26.04 is not affected. It has podman 5.7.0 with crun 1.21 at /usr/bin/crun.

### Expected behavior

podman runs containers on the ubuntu-24.04 image.

### Actual behavior

Every container fails to start with `unknown version specified`, because podman uses /usr/bin/crun 1.14.1 rather than the 1.28 shipped in /usr/local/bin.

### Repro steps

```yaml
jobs:
  repro:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - run: |
          podman --version
          podman info --format '{{.Host.OCIRuntime.Path}}'
          /usr/bin/crun --version
          /usr/local/bin/crun --version
          podman run --rm docker.io/library/alpine echo hello
```

This fails when the job lands on 20260726.254.1. The `Image Version:` line in the "Set up job" group shows which image the run actually got.

```

On the broken runner, this selects `/usr/local/bin/crun` 1.28 instead of the stale `/usr/bin/crun` 1.14.1 selected by Podman’s built-in runtime search. It also remains compatible with previous runner images.

title: [Ubuntu 24.04] podman 5.8.4 bundle: `podman exec` into a running container never returns
body:
### Description

Since the podman 5.8.4 static bundle replaced the apt package in
`images/ubuntu/scripts/build/install-container-tools.sh`, `podman exec` into a
running container can hang forever. Not slow — it never returns. The container
is up and healthy, the exec just never completes.

It does not happen on every exec. In our CI roughly 1 job in 3 wedges, always on
an exec, and once wedged it stays wedged until the step timeout kills it. Jobs
that had no step timeout held a runner for 6 hours.

The hung process is in userspace, not the kernel. No process is in
uninterruptible sleep. `podman` sits on a futex:

```
--- pid 3507 (podman) state=S wchan=0 ---
[<0>] futex_do_wait+0x3a/0x70
[<0>] __futex_wait+0x99/0x100
[<0>] futex_wait+0x72/0x120
[<0>] do_futex+0xc9/0x190
[<0>] __x64_sys_futex+0x125/0x1f0
[<0>] x64_sys_call+0x1d1d/0x20d0
[<0>] do_syscall_64+0x7b/0xb40
```

Its `conmon` is in a normal `ppoll`, and `fuse-overlayfs` is in a normal
`fuse_dev_do_read`. Neither is stuck. That points at a lock inside podman

title: Ubuntu 24.04 (20261004.327.1): UDP 127.0.0.1:53 cannot be bound on westus2 hosted runners since 2026-10-12, other regions unaffected
body:
### Description

Since 2026-10-12 at about 18:38 UTC, jobs that land on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runners in Azure region `westus2` behave differently from the same image in every other region: a process that restarts `systemd-resolved` and then binds UDP `127.0.0.1:53` fails with `failed to listen`.

For us that process is the StepSecurity harden-runner agent, which then reverts its changes and restarts Docker, killing the job's service containers. That part is reported to them as step-security/harden-runner#705. This issue is about the runner side: the image version did not change, yet behaviour on one region did.

I am not sure this tracker is the right place, since the evidence points at the `westus2` fleet and not at image contents. If it belongs elsewhere, please point me there.

### Platforms affected

- [ ] Azure DevOps
- [x] GitHub Actions - Standard Runners
- [ ] GitHub Actions - Larger Runners

### Runner images affected

- [x] Ubuntu 24.04

### Image version and build link

Image `ubuntu-24.04`, version `20261004.327.1`. Runner `2.337.0`, Hosted Compute Agent `20261002.596`, Docker API `1.48`. The repository is private, so I cannot link builds here; I can share run and job IDs.

### Is it regression?

Yes in behaviour, but not in image version: the same image version `20261004.327.1` ran in `westus2` without this failure until 12 October about 18:30 UTC, and still runs without it in every other region.

### Expected behavior

The same image behaves the same in every region: after `systemctl restart systemd-resolved`, UDP `127.0.0.1:53` can be bound, as it can on `centralus`, `eastus`, `eastus2`, `westus`, `westus3` and the others.

### Actual behavior

On `westus2` the bind fails. Counts from 692 job logs between 3 and 13 October, region taken from the `Region:` line in the job log:

| Runner region | Jobs before 12 Oct 18:30 UTC / bind failures | Jobs after / bind failures |
|---|---|---|
| `westus2` | 33 / 0 | 27 / 24 |
| ten other regions | 446 / 0 | 186 / 0 |

Sequence on an affected runner (UTC, 13 October):

```
11:43:23 sudo: COMMAND=/usr/bin/systemctl stop systemd-resolved
11:43:23 sudo: COMMAND=/usr/bin/systemctl restart systemd-resolved
11:43:23 sudo: COMMAND=/usr/bin/resolvectl flush-caches
11:43:23 sudo: COMMAND=/usr/bin/systemctl reload docker
11:43:24 sudo: COMMAND=/usr/bin/systemctl restart docker
11:43:26 agentservice: failed to listen on &{127.0.0.1:53 udp <nil> <nil> ...
```

The job log does not show what holds the port.

### Repro steps

title: [Ubuntu 26.04] `/tmp` is now a RAM-backed tmpfs with a ~7.8G per-user quota; large builds fail with "disk quota exceeded"
body:
### Description

On ubuntu-26.04, `/tmp` is a `tmpfs` (RAM disk) instead of a directory on the root disk.
It is mounted with size=50% of RAM (~7.8G on standard runners) and the `usrquota` option.

Tools that write large temporary files to `/tmp` now fail, even though the root disk
has ~90G free. For example, `go build` uses `/tmp` for its work directory by default.
For example, a large Go build (OpenTelemetry Collector contrib distribution) fails with:

```
compile: writing output: write $WORK/b4822/_pkg_.a: disk quota exceeded
```

The same build passes on ubuntu-24.04, where `/tmp` is on the root disk.

This comes from Ubuntu 26.04 itself: it now ships systemd's upstream tmp.mount unit
("the /tmp directory is now a tmpfs file system by default"):
https://documentation.ubuntu.com/release-notes/26.04/summary-for-lts-users/

The change is not mentioned in the Ubuntu 26.04 GA announcement (#14747), the
`ubuntu-latest` migration announcement (#14748), or the image README. Many workflows
will hit this when `ubuntu-latest` moves to 26.04 in November 2026.

Request, one of:
1. Mount `/tmp` on the root disk (for example, mask `tmp.mount` in the image), to keep 24.04 behavior, or
2. At least document the change and its size/quota limits in the announcements and the README,

body:
### Description

I'm not sure if it's really a bug, but it cost me a couple of hours, so I'd like to at least leave a record of it somewhere where it can be found and, maybe, understand why is accessing https://debuginfod.ubuntu.com from GitHub Actions runners so slow.

Anyhow, the facts that motivated this are:

1. A relatively [recent run](https://github.com/SOCI/soci/actions/runs/28614100942/job/84853488049) of the CI job using Valgrind to run tests finished in 106 seconds. In case the log times out, here is the important part:
```
    1/4 Test #1: soci_empty_test ..................   Passed    2.20 sec
```
i.e. the test using "empty" database backend not doing anything took ~2s. This run used ubuntu-24.04 image version 20260628.225.1 and ran on the host compute agent with version 20260624.560 and ran on July 2.

2. All the subsequent runs of exactly the same workflow, using the same commit, starting from July 24 and until the latest commit, timed out because Valgrind ran extremely slowly. Here is an excerpt from a [recent run](https://github.com/SOCI/soci/actions/runs/31523383040/job/93885711625) which ran today, August 11, on ubuntu-24.04 image version 20260720.247.2 and host compute agent version 20260707.563. The "empty" test still succeeds but look at the time it takes now:
```
    1/4 Test #1: soci_empty_test ..................   Passed  813.81 sec
```

title: devenv.com hangs indefinitely on its first invocation on a fresh windows-11-arm64 runner
body:
### Description

The first invocation of `devenv.com` on a freshly-provisioned `windows-11-arm64` runner hangs indefinitely with zero output, even for a trivial project build with no extensions involved. This surfaced while debugging a CMake issue where `check_language(Fortran)` invokes `devenv.com` to identify a Fortran compiler under the Visual Studio generator (see [cmake#28101](https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/28101) context), but the hang reproduces with a bare, direct `devenv.com` call, entirely outside of CMake.

Isolated repro: [workflow run](https://github.com/jmarrec/test-Github-Actions/actions/runs/35715407468/job/106705612721#step:3:33) — a PowerShell step calls

```
devenv.com CompilerIdFortran_arm64.vfproj /build Debug
```

as the very first Visual-Studio-touching action on the runner. Attempt 1 produces **zero stdout/stderr** and is still running when force-killed by our own 60s external timeout. Every subsequent invocation of the exact same command on the same VM (attempts 2-10) completes in a few seconds with normal output.

This matches the pattern reported in #13398, where a first-run feedback/survey dialog appears after installing a VS extension and blocks `devenv.com` from exiting until manually dismissed — except here it reproduces with no extension installed at all, just on the very first `devenv.com` launch per VM.


**Note:** this first attempt failure does not occur 100% of the time. I haven't run a thousand times to get meaningful statistics but it looks like it happens about 60% of the time. the x64 version always works.

Since image `ubuntu24/20260804.265`, mounting any FUSE filesystem the normal unprivileged way fails: the setuid-root `fusermount3` helper's `mount(2)` call returns `EPERM`. The identical call succeeds when `fusermount3` is invoked by root, and non-FUSE root mounts (e.g. tmpfs) work fine. This breaks FUSE-based CI generally (libfuse tools such as sshfs/rclone, Rust `fuser`, AppImage, fuse-overlayfs) whenever the job runs as the `runner` user.

Ruled out on a failing VM:

- `/usr/bin/fusermount3` is setuid (`-rwsr-xr-x root:root`), `/dev/fuse` present (`crw-rw-rw-`), stock `/etc/fuse.conf`
- No AppArmor profile for fusermount3 exists and `dmesg` shows zero denials; `Seccomp: 0`, `NoNewPrivs: 0`, full `CapBnd`
- Distro packages are unchanged vs the working image (`fuse3` 3.14.0-5build1, `apparmor` 4.0.1really4.0.1-0ubuntu0.24.04.7)

The only relevant delta is the kernel: `6.17.0-1020-azure` (works) → `6.17.0-1021-azure` (fails). strace of the user-invoked helper (root strace with `-u` so setuid semantics are preserved):

```
mount("/dev/fuse", ".", "fuse", MS_NOSUID|MS_NODEV, "fd=3,rootmode=40000,user_id=1001"...) = -1 EPERM (Operation not permitted)
```

The same mount performed by real root returns 0. Behaviorally, the new kernel appears to reject fuse mounts when the caller's *real* uid is unprivileged, even with euid 0 and full capabilities.

Both image versions are currently serving `ubuntu-latest`, so the failure appears intermittent run-to-run.

Broken: `20260804.265` / `20260804.265.1` ([release](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/releases/tag/ubuntu24%2F20260804.265)). Working: `20260720.247.2`. (Affected runs are in a private repository; self-contained repro below.)

### Is it regression?

Yes. Works on `ubuntu24/20260720.247.2` (kernel `6.17.0-1020-azure`).

Unprivileged processes can mount FUSE filesystems through the setuid `fusermount3` helper, as on all previous images.

### Actual behavior

title: [Ubuntu 24.04] Cached Node.js 22.x is 22.23.0 (undici "Premature close" regression) — plan to bump to 22.23.1+?
body:
### Description

The Ubuntu 24.04 hosted image ships **Node.js 22.23.0** in the tool cache
(`/opt/hostedtoolcache/node/22.23.0/x64`). With `actions/setup-node` and
`node-version: 22` (the default `check-latest: false`), workflows resolve to
this cached 22.23.0 rather than the latest 22.x.

Node 22.23.0 contains a keep-alive / socket-reuse regression that surfaces as
`ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` ("Premature close") for HTTP clients that reuse
pooled connections (e.g. `gaxios` → Google STS/OAuth endpoints). It was fixed
in **Node 22.23.1**.

Upstream tracking issue (documented on the 24.x line, same regression class):
https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/63989

title: macos-15-intel can't reach api.apple-cloudkit.com, notarization stapling fails with Error 68 since Oct 12

### Description

Since Oct 12, stapling notarization tickets fails most of the time on macos-15-intel. Apple accepts the notarization fine, but when xcrun stapler fetches the ticket from api.apple-cloudkit.com the connection is dropped after about 7 seconds and it exits with Error 68. Calls that work finish in under half a second, and both happen within the same job.

We've re-run our release six times between Oct 12 16:08 UTC and Oct 13 07:10 UTC, each on a different machine, and all six failed this way. The same workflow on macos-14 (arm64), also in westus, staples without any problem. notarytool submit/status works fine from the Intel runners, and the same CloudKit request returns 200 from outside GitHub, so it looks like the network path from the Intel runners to Apple.

The dropped connections went to 17.248.191.13, 17.248.228.27, 17.248.194.15 and 17.250.48.41 on port 443. We also saw codesign fail once to reach Apple's timestamp server.

title: Error: failed to open 2048 locks in /libpod_lock: numerical result out of range
body:
### Description

Users who install Podman via APT (currently version 4.9.3 in Ubuntu Noble) in ARM images will get the following error when running any subsequent Podman command:

```
Error: failed to open 2048 locks in /libpod_lock: numerical result out of range
```

The underlying cause is that Podman 5.8.4 is already installed in the runner image via other means, leading to two different Podman versions in the same VM. Normally this would not be an issue, but the installation of Podman via APT creates a `/dev/shm/libpod_lock` file that is not compatible with Podman 5.8.4. title: `make` shouldn't be an alias for `mingw32-make`
body:
### Description

Currently, when installing mingw, [you copy `mingw32-make.exe` to `make.exe`](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/c47d2b0e05c0caa3d66b4a445968af94baf61399/images/windows/scripts/build/Install-Mingw64.ps1#L34).

I suggest that this shouldn't be done.

Those are two different flavors of Make with different bugs/quirks, and non-trivial makefiles written for one will not work with another. When I see `make.exe` on Windows, my expectation is that it's Cygwin-based, which is e.g. what MSYS2 does (they have both Cygwin-based `make.exe` and MinGW-based `mingw32-make.exe`).

We just spent some time debugging a misbehaving makefile, only to realize that we accidentally ran it using the preinstalled `make.exe` (which is `mingw32-make.exe` in disguise) rather than MSYS2 `make.exe`.

Here's [an example of a `mingw32-make`-specific quirk](https://github.com/msys2/mingw-packages/issues/17735), it's the one we ran into. The annoying part is that I knew about this, but figured that it couldn't be affecting us since we weren't invoking `mingw32-make` explicitly.

 ubuntu-22.04 in a side-by-side run.

`macos-26` is ready to become the default version for the `macos-latest` label in GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps.

### Target date

This change will be rolled out over a period of several weeks beginning of June, 15th 2026. We plan to complete the migration by July 15th 2026.
